method: read-only static inspection of the productive sources plus repository-wide alias search; no productive module imported, no pipeline executed

stagesInspected.note: contourEngine.js:509 only mentions holes in a comment about separate regions sewn over a fill
semanticSegmenter.js:230 mentions holes only inside an LLM complexity prompt (1-5 scale)

producer.inputUsed: the sibling region array (allRegions): other.id, other.centroid (normalized 0-1), other.area_mm2; plus this region's own area_mm2 and centroid
producer.formula: count(other.id !== self.id && other.centroid && other.area_mm2 < 0.12 * self.area_mm2 && hypot(other.centroid - self.centroid) < 0.15)
producer.preservedRecomputedOrOverwritten: recomputed and written on every enrichRegion call; no upstream stage supplies a competing value, so nothing earlier is preserved
producer.meaningPlainText: how many OTHER regions of the same design are both small relative to this one (< 12 % of its area) and centroid-near (< 0.15 normalized units)

meaningClassification.otherSemantics: inter-region proximity heuristic between sibling regions

consumers.use: computeQuality subtracts 8 quality points per unit and pushes an advisory issue
eiePriority forces priority 10 for running_stitch when the value is > 0
copies the scalar into its geo payload
sums it into the explicitHoleCount benchmark metric

conclusions: the field name is misleading: the producer never inspects the region's own boundary
no interior ring, child contour, contour hierarchy or Euler number is computed anywhere in the productive pipeline
no productive field stores hole boundary geometry, so no consumer could sew or knock out an interior hole
therefore a value > 0 does not certify a topological interior hole
